bodyMarkdown:
## Definition

Progressive specification is the principle that design decisions become more specific as work moves from research to requirements to specifications to system. Early work stays at a higher level of abstraction. Later work resolves detail as understanding increases.

Progressive specification treats specificity as earned through exploration. It avoids locking in detailed decisions before the terrain is understood.

## The problem progressive specification addresses

Progressive specification addresses the risk of premature specificity. When a full system is specified at the start of an engagement, the specification is based on initial understanding rather than on what later research reveals.

The contrasting pattern is front-loaded specification. In front-loaded specification, the full system is specified at the start of the engagement. The risk is that the engagement's own research then contradicts the specification.

## How specificity increases through exploration

Progressive specification separates exploration from specification. Early phases explore rather than specify. Specificity is not assumed upfront; it is built as the work clarifies what the system needs to be.

This means that design decisions become progressively more resolved as the engagement moves through phases. The movement is sequential: research, then requirements, then specifications, then system.

## Progressive specification in architectural iteration

Progressive specification is reflected in the four-iteration architecture approach. Each iteration of structural deliverables produces a more specific version of the architecture.

Iteration 1 is described as broad logic. Iteration 4 is described as detailed optimisation. The principle is that architecture becomes more specific as understanding increases.

## Relationship to organic system building

Progressive specification is related to organic system building. The relationship is that specificity cannot be imposed on a system that has not yet revealed what it needs to be.

Progressive specification is the mechanism by which specificity is built without being imposed. It allows the system definition to become more precise as the work uncovers the system's needs.

## Boundary with front-loaded specification

Progressive specification differs from front-loaded specification in where detail is placed. Progressive specification delays detailed resolution until the work has produced enough understanding to support it.

Front-loaded specification places full system detail at the beginning. The limitation of that pattern is that early assumptions may be contradicted by later research.

## Evidence basis and limits

Progressive specification is established as a strategic concept and is supported by its relationships to exploration, architectural iteration, and organic system building. The available treatment is conceptual rather than evidence-heavy.

Detailed case examples, implementation rules, and a full methodology treatment are not established here. The concept should therefore be used as a principle of staged specificity, not as a complete process description.

## Related pages

Organic system building is the closest related concept because progressive specification describes how specificity is built without being imposed before the system has revealed what it needs to be.
